sources.quote: One Dutch company: NAI Logistics B.V.; One Bulgarian company: Lego Investments EOOD
sources.searcher_note: The designation itself: NAI Logistics B.V. listed as owned/controlled by Ajmal Rahmani. Says nothing about any DoD contracts or payments to NAI Logistics B.V.

sources.quote: rigging bids, and eliminating competition on U.S.-funded contracts
sources.searcher_note: Same page, second quote: the scheme the Rahmanis were sanctioned for is fuel-contract fraud on U.S.-funded Afghan contracts, not the Dutch company's DoD payments.

sources.outlet: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia (Rahmani v. Yellen, No. 24-0285)
sources.quote: Plaintiffs say that A. Rahmani's companies did not participate in fuel contracts after 2017.
sources.searcher_note: Possible disagreement: the Rahmanis' own claim, as recounted by the court, that their companies left fuel contracting after 2017. Names NAI Energy Europe and NAI Management among plaintiffs, not NAI Logistics B.V.

sources.quote: In 2014, the Rahmanis and other companies involved in fuel business colluded to drive up prices in the US-funded contracts for as much as $200 million.
sources.searcher_note: News coverage of the sanctions and the fuel-contract scheme; does not name NAI Logistics B.V. or any post-sanction DoD payment.

sources.quote: During the war in Afghanistan, Rahmani and his father worked as major contractors supplying fuel and other services to NATO forces.
sources.searcher_note: Rahmani family as NATO fuel contractors and their fight against the sanctions; no mention of NAI Logistics B.V. or DoD payments after designation.

notes: No source found that reports DoD/DLA payments to NAI Logistics B.V., before or after the 2023-12-11 designation. The only source naming NAI Logistics B.V. is the Treasury designation list. GovTribe vendor page for NAI Logistics B.V. (https://govtribe.com/vendors/nai-logistics-b-dot-v-dot-h2g78) returned 403 and is a data mirror, not coverage; not recorded. OCCRP's 'Pentagon Fuel Subcontractor Owned by Alleged Front for U.S.-Blacklisted Brothers' is about the Lebanese Rahme brothers, a different network, not recorded. The Treasury page is recorded twice for two distinct quotes; it is one source.
